strengths: Novel weight graph representation that preserves network topology rather than flattening weights, with principled design based on forward data flow through network architecture

Well-motivated functional loss (Eq. 4) for VAE training that measures output consistency rather than parameter similarity, addressing the insight that functionally similar weights may differ parametrically
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 PDE systems and real-world ERA5 data with extensive ablation studies (weight representation, two-stage vs single-stage, component necessity)
Significant practical efficiency gains with ~3× faster test-time adaptation compared to meta-learning baselines and linear scaling of generator parameters with model size
Model-agnostic framework demonstrated on multiple architectures (FNO, UNO, WNO) with good extrapolation and unseen equation generalization results
Thorough robustness evaluation including permutation invariance, extrapolation, and sensitivity to observation length, plus statistical significance testing
Excellent explainability analysis (Figures 7-9) showing attention patterns align with network hierarchy and interpretable feature extraction from observations
weaknesses: Statistical significance issues: improvements on Lambda-Omega system are not significant (p=0.15 in-domain, p=0.53 out-domain); Kolmogorov only approaches significance (p=0.016 out-domain), undermining core claims

Catastrophic unexplained failures of baseline methods: D2NWG and CVAE fail 50-400× worse on some systems (e.g., CVAE achieves 4.454 RMSE on Kolmogorov vs 0.077 for DynaDiff); no investigation of whether this reflects unfair comparison, implementation bugs, or hyperparameter tuning disparity

Theoretical analysis in Appendix G makes unvalidated assumptions (particularly Assumption 1 on Functional Lipschitz Continuity) and uses auxiliary loss as informal 'tractable surrogate' rather than rigorously justified component; bounds don't account for model zoo construction

Fundamental limitation of fixed architecture generation not addressed despite acknowledgment; method cannot adapt architecture to environmental complexity, restricting applicability compared to alternatives

Model zoo design choices poorly justified: 100 models appears arbitrary with limited ablation; domain-adaptive initialization affects learned joint distribution but treated as implementation detail rather than fundamental design choice

Prompter design concerns: hand-crafted physical features (mean, variance, energy, enstrophy) lack sensitivity analysis; Table 13 shows minimal difference using actual vs. learned environment, suggesting prompter may not be learning substantively

Inconsistent baseline comparisons with extreme performance variance across methods and systems not explained; raises concerns about experimental setup consistency or fair implementation of competing methods

strengths: Novel generative paradigm for cross-environment weight adaptation using diffusion models, positioning weights as a data modality
Well-motivated technical choices: weight graphs preserve architectural structure, functional loss addresses weight-output similarity mismatch
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple PDE systems with extensive ablations and interpretability analysis
Demonstrates competitive or superior performance to One-per-Env upper bound on some systems
Detailed supplementary material with theoretical analysis and robustness studies
weaknesses: Misleading problem framing: claims to address 'data-scarce' scenarios but requires training 100 expert models per training environment (substantial hidden cost), undermining the main motivation
Statistical significance not established: results are significant only on 50% of systems (Table 5: Lambda-Omega p=0.15-0.53, Kolmogorov p=0.49), contradicting the abstract's 10.78% improvement claim

Incomplete baseline comparisons: parameter count fairness not addressed systematically; D2NWG/CVAE catastrophic failures suggest potential implementation issues; baseline scaling analysis limited to 2 methods
Generalization error analysis (Appendix G) relies on three unvalidated assumptions and provides no quantitative, testable bounds or insights
Domain-specific prompter design with hand-crafted features (mean, variance, energy, enstrophy) limits generalizability to new domain types; no ablation on prompter components
Fixed architecture limitation severely constrains generalization; framework cannot adapt architectures to new environments, contradicting the 'complete model generation' framing
Computational efficiency claims overstated: test-time speed advantage only vs. meta-learning methods (not One-per-Env); 3× speedup requires pre-computed expensive model zoo
Weak ablations: two-stage vs. single-stage ablation lacks mechanistic insight; no comparison of weight graphs to simpler flattened-weight baselines; functional loss coefficient untuned

strengths: Novel generative paradigm for weight adaptation: Shifting from gradient-based fine-tuning to directly modeling p(θ|e) is conceptually important and well-motivated, particularly for data-scarce settings

Technical innovations are sound and well-designed: Weight graphs preserve architectural structure via attention mechanisms, functional loss captures behavioral similarity rather than parameter similarity, and the dynamics-informed prompter elegantly combines domain knowledge with learned spectral features

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 4 PDE systems plus real-world ERA5 data, extensive baseline comparisons (6 foundation models + 6 meta-learning + 2 weight generation methods), thorough ablations (4.5, J.4-J.6), and advanced analysis including extrapolation robustness, unseen equations, and permutation invariance
Practical efficiency: Achieves 3× faster test-time adaptation than meta-learning baselines while improving accuracy by 10.78% on average; enables deployment on resource-constrained systems
Excellent reproducibility: 28 pages of supplementary material with complete implementation details, hyperparameters, architecture specifications, and data generation procedures
Model-agnostic framework: Demonstrated extensibility across FNO, WNO, and UNO with minimal performance variation, validating the generality of the approach
Interpretability analysis: Attention visualizations (Section 4.3) convincingly show the model learns meaningful architectural hierarchies and functional module structure without explicit supervision
Honest limitation discussion: Clearly acknowledges fixed architecture constraint and model zoo construction overhead
weaknesses: Inconsistent statistical significance: Lambda-Omega system shows no significant improvements (p > 0.05 in both in- and out-domain); Kolmogorov Flow in-domain also not significant (p = 0.49). Claim of 'consistent performance across all systems' is overstated given mixed results

Fixed architecture limitation severely restricts practical applicability: Framework can only generate weights for a single fixed architecture, whereas real applications often require different architectures for different problems. This is acknowledged but inadequately addressed

Substantial model zoo construction overhead: Requires training 100 expert models offline (18GB storage and significant computational cost per Table 4). Comparison fairness questionable since foundation models don't require this preprocessing; total cost (Table 16) is non-trivial despite being offline

Framework complexity with unclear component contributions: Method combines weight graphs, attention VAE, latent diffusion, and physics-informed prompter with many interdependencies. While ablations help, sensitivity to hyperparameters across four major subsystems is not fully characterized

Theoretical analysis relies on unvalidated assumptions: Assumptions 1-3 (Appendix G) are stated but not rigorously justified. Assumption 1 (Lipschitz continuity) relies on vague appeal to 'smooth nature of diffusion' without formal proof. The resulting bound is loose and provides limited quantitative guidance

Prompter design suggests incomplete physics extraction: Auxiliary loss L_aux requires ground-truth environment parameters e, and while ablation shows only marginal improvement, its necessity suggests the base prompter may not extract sufficient physical information without supervision

Comparison with oracle One-per-Env is unsatisfying: Figure 3 shows DynaDiff sometimes beats the oracle, attributed to local optima. Unclear whether generated models learn the true distribution or are simply better regularized solutions

Limited scope and scale: All experiments use small expert models (~1M parameters). Unclear how framework scales to modern large models (100M+). Evaluation limited to classical dynamical systems without modern applications

Reproducibility concerns for practitioners: Requires careful tuning of model zoo construction, many hyperparameters (15+ for VAE/diffusion), and no code availability mentioned despite complex implementation
